notes: EMERGENCY BOUND DELIVERED; DIAGNOSIS TRANSFERRED TO T335. Symptom: `zig build test` never finished. Five test binaries were found alive at ~100% CPU with 100-171 minutes of accumulated CPU each and machine load average 16; killing them freed a core only until the next console ran the suite. Evidence is a sampled stack (macOS `sample`, PID 5857): test_runner -> qa023_brute_2x2.test."smoke: empty board Black to move -> value 0 (published anchor)" -> value (qa023_brute_2x2.zig:235) -> brute_value recursing between :211 (pass branch) and :221 (placement branch) without unwinding. Mechanism, which is NOT an infinite loop: the cycle check at the head of brute_value rejects only repeats along the CURRENT PATH, so the search enumerates simple paths rather than memoising; with branching <=5 and DEPTH_LIMIT=64 the worst case is ~5^64 nodes. It stayed cheap only while most lines terminated early. Fix applied at 00bd3cb: a 20,000,000-node budget that @panics with a named message, converting an unbounded spin into a fast loud failure. Verified: the test now terminates in seconds with exit 1 (signal ABRT) and prints the T360 panic text; before the change it ran for hours. The budget is deliberately NOT a fix for the underlying explosion and the panic text says so. OPEN QUESTION, handed to T335 because it concerns its kernel: why did the search space explode today when the suite passed at 12:40 (EXIT=0, 3:31 wall)? Hypothesis A, mine, now WEAKENED: T339's kernel extraction changed 2x2 move or terminal semantics - but `git show --stat 2062d82` is 505 insertions and ZERO deletions, purely additive, so existing call paths should be untouched. Hypothesis B, better: qa023_brute_2x2 was an orphaned test that nothing executed, and the sprint's build.zig wiring pulled it into a test binary for the first time, in which case it is not a regression but a never-run test that was always this expensive. Method given to T335: bisect rules.zig at 2062d82, and check whether that test ran in the suite before today. Do not edit the test until the answer is known. Process note for the record: the Orchestrator dismissed a worker's correct report that the suite hangs (T338 closed --skip-acceptance citing it) after observing 99% CPU for thirty seconds and concluding 'compute-bound, not hung' - compute-bound is exactly what this looks like from outside, and the worker was right about the symptom while naming the wrong function.
